stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time t minutes is \( x(t) = - t \left(t - 5\right)^{2} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 10 \). Find all open intervals of time in \( 0 < t < 10 \) during which the particle is moving to the right. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(\frac{5}{3}, 5\right) \), because \( v(t) > 0 \) there.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the position with the product rule: \( v(t) = x'(t) = - \left(t - 5\right) \left(3 t - 5\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) gives \( t = \frac{5}{3}, 5 \), which split \( 0 < t < 10 \) into pieces on which v keeps one sign.

Testing a time in each piece shows \( v(t) > 0 \) exactly on \( \left(\frac{5}{3}, 5\right) \). The particle moves to the right when its velocity is positive, so it moves to the right on \( \left(\frac{5}{3}, 5\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of velocity gives the direction of motion

options.label: The particle is never moving to the right for \( 0 < t < 10 \), because \( x(t) > 0 \) at no time in that interval.
options.derivation: the direction read from the sign of the position x(t) rather than of the velocity

options.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(0, \frac{10}{3}\right) \), because v(t) is increasing there.
options.derivation: the direction read from whether the velocity is increasing, the sign of its change, rather than from its sign
